name: Full planner decision
description: The orchestrator's own planner makes one planning call and its decision is the route. The call sees the message and a quest view and can return a tool with arguments, a deep brief, a confirm or a clarify. Only the planning step runs in the measured arm; nothing is executed.
advantages: Returns a real decision with arguments, confirm and clarify handling, and the context to brief a deep run or ground an answer. It is what production uses, so the measurement is of the live behaviour. Selected because: core/orchestrator_planning.py (PLANNER_PROFILES). A QAR lane runs the pre-route stage first (core/pre_route.py, owned by operate-a-quest, whose default is pre_route) and this planner decides every message the pre-route does not settle; quest-backend passes no pre-router, so Quest chat runs the planner alone
disadvantages: Every message pays for a planning call even when the request is plainly a simple tool use. Its rubric is long and has shown specific misses, such as sending a paraphrased state update to the wrong route and not confirming a mass destructive request.

name: Keyword rules floor
description: Hand-written regular expressions map message wording to a route and tool with no model call: deep-work words send to deep, a few phrasings map to named tools, negations such as do not save map to answer, and the rest are answers. It is the baseline any model-based router must beat to justify its cost.
advantages: Free, instant, deterministic and easy to audit, and it makes a meaningful floor for judging whether a model call earns its cost.
disadvantages: It cannot fill arguments, handle multi-step requests, paraphrase or negation beyond its patterns, or confirm a destructive ask. Each new phrasing needs a new rule, so coverage decays as users word things differently.

name: Stream, milestone and fan-out sinks
description: The stream sink forwards every event to the consumer's stream, the milestone sink forwards only the always-surfacing event types to named callbacks, and the fan-out sink sends live events to both and supports detaching the live side. A failing forward or callback never breaks the run.
advantages: Policy lives in one place so every consumer inherits it, and failures in a consumer cannot stop the work. Selected because: Mode selects StreamSink or MilestoneSink
disadvantages: Policy is fixed by event type, so a consumer wanting a different split must write a sink, and swallowed failures can hide a dead stream.

name: Sink policy cases
description: Builds the production sinks and feeds them event sequences for live, background, handoff and broken-stream cases, recording what each surfaced.
advantages: Offline and deterministic, and exercises the real sinks, including the failure paths.
disadvantages: Scores the sinks only; it cannot say whether the orchestrator emits the right events.

name: Live recipe replay arm
description: The orchestrator with a recipe store and the real model: the first success teaches a recipe, and a later matching request replays the tool call before any context search through one fill-arguments call.
advantages: Measures the real cost and correctness benefit with a real model, changing only the recipe store against the baseline. Selected because: RunnerConfig.recipe_store
disadvantages: Needs the model CLI and spends tokens; built but not recorded, so the real-model result is missing.

name: Live planner-only baseline
description: The normal path with no recipe store: plan, search context, call the tool, reply, with one orchestrator for the whole run.
advantages: The correctness reference every recipe approach must match, and it needs no learning state.
disadvantages: Pays a full planning and search cost on every repeat; unrecorded for lack of an approved model run.

name: Offline recipe replay arm
description: The live orchestrator and live recipe store over a fake tool world with a deterministic rule model standing in for the model, so the replay engine (nominate, fill arguments, mutating guard, learning) is exercised with its real model-call count.
advantages: Offline, free and repeatable, and shows fewer model calls at the same pass rate.
disadvantages: The rule model is an optimistic ceiling written with the cases in view, so it does not show real model judgment.

name: Offline planner-only baseline
description: The same orchestrator, fake world and rule model with no recipe store, so every request takes the full path.
advantages: Gives the exact like-for-like count of model calls to compare against, at no cost.
disadvantages: Shares the rule model's optimism and so only checks parity and call count, not real behaviour.

name: Live assembly-point driver
description: Drives the real planner prompt builder with a capture provider, plus the real autopilot batch composer, context-update block renderer and deep goal prompt composer, and reports size and duplicates for each fixture.
advantages: Measures what the live paths really produce with no model calls, and covers four assembly points. Selected because: live paths: Orchestrator._plan, autopilot_briefs.compose_batch_text, ContextUpdates.as_prompt_block, goal_runner_contract.compose_goal_prompt (fitted by core/prompt_budget.py)
disadvantages: Fixtures are synthetic filler, and budgets are partly policy, so it checks size, not whether the prompt holds the right content.

name: Milestone sink
description: A background sink that surfaces only result, decision, milestone, context and done events to named callbacks.
advantages: A quiet default for background work: the person sees outcomes and decisions only.
disadvantages: A consumer wanting a different split must write a sink.

name: Classify through the message router alternatives
description: Quest classification of a request (answer, tool, deep, confirm, clarify, and the tool and arguments) is done by the four recorded alternatives of route-a-message (full planner, cheap pre-route then planner, single prompt, keyword rules), scored on the classification cases.
advantages: Four real alternatives already exist and are compared on the labelled classification cases by one scorer; no new code.
disadvantages: Covers classifying a message, not choosing which quest an ask belongs to or recommending the next goal, step or quest; those two tasks still lack labelled cases and an alternative.

name: Route with the registry of examples, by model tier
description: The backend's intent routing conditioned on a registry of labelled examples, run on the cheapest tier or a stronger one, with or without the registry (quest-backend qar_eval/intent_routing.py; arms registry_haiku and registry_sonnet).
advantages: Recorded in quest-backend esoi/quest-ai/results.csv on its held-out and registry cases: haiku scores the same as sonnet at about a third of the cost.
disadvantages: Backend-side and a small case set in the recorded run; not yet run on which-quest or recommendation cases.

name: Fixed status line, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. The first beat is a fixed line chosen from the turn's mode and first event, with no model call.
advantages: No cost and no delay.
disadvantages: Says less about this turn; not built.

name: One model call writes the explanation from the trace (today)
description: After a turn that answered, a structured call writes the explanation from the trace at the configured explanation tier.
advantages: Built; the only arm that makes the model call.
disadvantages: Not measured; its cost, time and value are unknown until the metric is built.

name: Template over the trace, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. The explanation is assembled from the trace entries by a fixed template, with no model call.
advantages: No cost, no delay, cannot invent a step.
disadvantages: Reads as a log, not as prose; not built.

name: Measured only on labelled rows
description: Reads the evaluation folders and the results log. A task counts as measured when the component it names has a case file with labelled expectations and its latest row for the named arm reads at or above the bar of the combined metric, and the result gives that recorded accuracy.
advantages: Costs no model call and reruns nothing. A task that names no component, a component with no cases, an arm never recorded or a row under the bar reads as not measured, so a task cannot be called measured because it is listed.
disadvantages: Only reads rows already recorded, so it is as current as the last run of each component. A task with no labelled case set fails on purpose until one exists, and it does not say whether the labels are good.

name: No task mapped to a measure
description: Reports every classification and recommendation task as not measured, as before this solution existed, whatever the folders and the log hold.
advantages: Costs nothing and sets the floor: any arm that reads the evidence must report more measured tasks than this one, and the check that separates the two is visible.
disadvantages: Says nothing about any task, so it is useful only as the baseline to beat.

name: Planner prompt with only the rules that apply to the turn
description: Builds the planner prompt for each turn from only the rules whose condition the turn's structured facts do not rule out (its mode, whether a deep runner is wired, the reach verdict, whether tools or material exist), and builds every other prompt as it is built in production. A fact the turn lacks keeps its rule.
advantages: Makes the planner prompt shorter for turns that need fewer rules, with no model call, and each case can be compared with the full text of the same turn. The facts come from structure the orchestrator holds, never from words the model wrote.
disadvantages: Opt-in, as the default stays the full prompt. It shows size and duplicate blocks only, not whether the model still decides well without the dropped rules, and a turn whose facts are unknown keeps most rules, so it saves little there.

name: Nothing shown (the status quo before the Trail)
description: The app shows no trace of the work: dots, then the answer.
advantages: Nothing to get wrong, nothing added to the screen. Selected because: not selected; it is the incumbent the others are measured against.
disadvantages: The person cannot see that the answer rests on real work, so a turn with work shows nothing.

name: A plain list of every step
description: One row per step in arrival order with every item listed under it, live and settled, whether or not the answer used it.
advantages: Complete, and nothing is hidden behind a tap.
disadvantages: Shows counts of internal work and items the answer did not use; a long run grows the page.

name: Behaviour before the build (no interim for an unmet attempt)
description: The unmet attempt sends no interim message (the earlier interim needed done evidence and analysis); the person gets the final answer only.
advantages: Nothing to get wrong. Selected because: not selected; the incumbent the others are measured against (a reconstruction).
disadvantages: The person cannot tell whether work continues.

name: An interim on every unmet attempt (spam baseline)
description: Every attempt that did not meet the goal sends an interim.
advantages: Never silent. Selected because: not selected; a baseline.
disadvantages: Repeats itself, sends before blockers that are not more work and ignores spacing and the cap.

name: The terminal draws the Trail from the hub's renderers
description: The chat terminal shows a live row of the newest page opened, a one-line summary of what was read that opens in place, interim updates folded into one row, an ask as a block answered by number or words, and a stopped reason with Continue. The rules and sentences are the hub's terminal renderers (the same words as the Quest app); QAR only draws their blocks, binds keys and sends the answer through the Quest client.
advantages: No second copy of the rules or the words in QAR; the Quest app's wording is checked against the hub's by a drift test. Selected because: not selected; it is the only terminal arm.
disadvantages: Drawn and tested headless only; never used by a person in a real terminal, and not measured on real turns. The interim updates need QAR_INTERIM_REPLIES=1. The terminal's turn still runs through QAR's own orchestrator, not a hub run function (none exists yet).

name: The planner prompt written by the real loop
description: The real planner builds the prompt for a message over a model that only records what it is asked, so the prompt is what the loop would send, with no model call.
advantages: Offline and free; shows exactly the text a step sends.
disadvantages: Covers the planner prompt only; the autopilot, context-update and deep-run prompts are measured by the live assembly-point driver.

name: The recipe store of the loop
description: Finds the recipes learned from earlier requests that a new request repeats, best first, from one JSON file or from memory.
advantages: Matching needs no model call, and a corrupt file reads as an empty store.
disadvantages: Matching is by shared words, so a paraphrase with none of them is missed.

name: Route read off the planner decision
description: The loop's planner makes its one planning call and the route is read off three fields of its decision by structure: a clarify action is clarify, a draft in the chat is draft, an act intent or a tool, deep or confirm action is act, anything else is information. Nothing is executed.
advantages: No extra call and the route cannot disagree with the plan; it is the route the loop has today.
disadvantages: Costs a full planning call per request and is only as good as the plan; the route is decided in the same place as the work.

name: One cheap classifier call
description: The hub's single classifier arm over the loop's cheap decision: one call picks information, act, draft or clarify from the request and the quest view, with no planning call.
advantages: One cheap call, independent of how the plan is made; reads what the person asks for.
disadvantages: A step before the plan that can disagree with it; not measured live yet.

name: Always information
description: The hub's floor: every request is information.
advantages: Free.
disadvantages: Misses every request that wants work, a draft or a question.

name: Run facts relay over the hub's data form (producer of the run-state ticks)
description: One relay per deep run reads the runner's events through the hub's adapter and folds them with the hub's frontend data form (the hub's Frontend Interface, arm json_wire) and structure view (the hub's Structure In View, arm event_tree), both reached through the front door. It hands the run's sink ordinary progress events that Quest stores and its screens draw: helpers with their parent and solution, the structure of the work, spend against the ceilings, the cost, the hub's own stop decision, and at the end the end reason, resume handle, spend, ceilings, what was touched outside the folder and what is left. The same relay serves a task (progress ticks and result_data) and a chat turn (events).
advantages: One producer for both surfaces, built on the hub's data form instead of hand-built dictionaries. A structure goes out only when the tree changed and a spend only after a gap, so the feed stays small. A fact the run does not know is left out, never sent as zero. Every tick shape is run through the backend's own validator in tests.
disadvantages: Seen only through fakes and the backend validator: nothing has been watched live in a browser or on a real Claude Code run. Solutions show as unknown ids until a consumer passes ESOI records. A run stopped at a limit is not verified, so what is left is not known and is left out. Helpers and cost come only from runners that report them on their stream.

name: Resume the stored session (the person's short message)
description: A short message such as Continue, read from the person's own words, continues the session the run that ended at a limit left (its resume handle) instead of starting over: a task takes the handle Quest hands back or its earlier report carried, a chat turn takes it from an in-memory ledger keyed by conversation. A resume with no handle is not claimed.
advantages: No change to Quest: Resume is the message its screens already send. Nothing a model wrote is read, and a finished run leaves nothing to resume.
disadvantages: The chat ledger is in memory, so a restart forgets it and the follow-up then starts as any other until Quest passes the stored handle itself. Recognition is a short list of sentences, so a screen that words Resume differently needs its sentence added.
